doc: A southern tropical storm (lat -14, radius 0.05) with float64 directions on a patch centered on it: the eye term in float64 rounded to float32. Tolerance rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-6 (the default): measured on this very case (a float64 patch around the storm, float32 output): a one-ulp nudge of every float64 direction (20 draws) and the squared distance recomputed in exact rational arithmetic both changed nothing after the cast to float32 (0 observed), because the eye exponent d2 / (0.12 r)^2 turns a 1e-16 error of d2 into only 3e-14; the float32-direction version of the same patch differs by 8.3e-7, which is why the float32 case has its own, looser tolerance. Conventions of cloudgen.sphere read here: lonlat_to_dir(lon, lat) = (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) with float64 numpy cos and sin (right-handed, z north, longitude grows east; a vortex center is that direction); normalize(v) = v / |v| (plain division, no epsilon: a zero vector gives NaN).

params.dtype_chain: p float64: d2, exp, the comma head and the eye are float64 per vortex; each vortex term is cast to float32 and accumulated in float32, in vortex order (float64 math per vortex, float32 accumulation). The output is float32.
